## Introduction

In the Devcontainers tutorial you examined a generic Python devcontainer and wrote a minimal R devcontainer from scratch. Now you will look at the devcontainer behind the Codespace you are working in right now. `codespace-starter` uses a custom image built specifically for this course, plus a detailed `settings` block that configures all of it.

## Codespace Starter Devcontainer

This section walks through `codespace-starter`'s `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` field by field: the custom image, the VS Code extensions, the settings, the `onCreateCommand` behind the ready banner, and the retired `postCreateCommand`. Unlike the minimal configurations from the Devcontainers tutorial, this one customizes almost everything so that every student gets an identical setup. The last few exercises install packages by hand, since everything the course itself needs is already baked into the image.

### Exercise 1
 
In the bash Terminal, run `cd /workspaces/codespace-starter`, then `code .devcontainer/devcontainer.json` to open the whole file in an editor tab. (The Explorer hides `.devcontainer` in `codespace-starter` to keep the starting view simple, but `code` opens any file by its path.) Find the line beginning with `"name"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-1
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "In the bash Terminal, run cd /workspaces/codespace-starter, then code .devcontainer/devcontainer.json to open the whole file in an editor tab. Find the line beginning with \"name\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"name": "Preceptor's Primer",
```

###

The `name` field is purely cosmetic --- it is the label GitHub shows for this configuration in the Codespace-creation picker and the VS Code window title.

### Exercise 2

Find the line beginning with `"image"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-2
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(

```

###

```{.output}
"image": "ghcr.io/ppbds/devcontainer:1.3.4",
```

###

`codespace-starter` uses a pinned version of a custom image, `ghcr.io/ppbds/devcontainer`, so every student gets the exact same setup, pre-loaded with Quarto, R, Python, the four course tutorial packages, and several AI tools.

### Exercise 3

Find the `"extensions"` array. Find the line containing `"reditorsupport.r"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-3
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Find the \"extensions\" array. Find the line containing \"reditorsupport.r\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"reditorsupport.r@3.0.1",
```

###

`reditorsupport.r` is the extension that gives VS Code R syntax highlighting, code completion, and the R Terminal. The `@3.0.1` **pins** it to one exact version. Without a pin, the Marketplace would update every student's Codespace the day a new release appeared. The comment above this line explains why that matters here. Version 3.0 of this extension changed how it attaches to a running R session, which is what gets plots into the plot pane, and it needs a matching R package, `sess`, that the image bakes in alongside this exact version. An uninvited update would have broken plotting mid-semester. Pinning lets the course decide *when* to take a change like that.

### Exercise 5

One extension is missing from the `"extensions"` array: `PPBDS.vscode-r-tutorials`, the extension this tutorial is running in. Find the `NOTE` comment just above the array that explains why it is not listed. Copy and paste the comment's first two lines.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-5
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "One extension is missing from the \"extensions\" array: PPBDS.vscode-r-tutorials, the extension this tutorial is running in. Find the NOTE comment just above the array that explains why it is not listed. Copy and paste the comment's first two lines.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
// NOTE — PPBDS.vscode-r-tutorials is deliberately NOT in this list.
// We publish it to Open VSX, and this list can only install from the
```

###

The `"extensions"` array can only install from the Microsoft Marketplace, and we publish `PPBDS.vscode-r-tutorials` to Open VSX. So it is baked into the image instead, through the `RT_EXT_VERSION` build argument in the PPBDS/devcontainers Dockerfile, pre-extracted so its Activity Bar icon exists from the first window paint.

### Exercise 6

Just below `"mechatroner.rainbow-csv"`, find the comment that begins `ALSO DELIBERATELY ABSENT`. Copy and paste its first four lines.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-6
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Just below \"mechatroner.rainbow-csv\", find the comment that begins ALSO DELIBERATELY ABSENT. Copy and paste its first four lines.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
// ALSO DELIBERATELY ABSENT (dropped 2026-08-20, David): the Python
// extensions (ms-python.python, ms-toolsai.jupyter). Students use
// only a handful of Activity Bar icons, and these two added Python/
// Jupyter icons plus Welcome-page walkthrough cards for tooling the
// course doesn't teach interactively. Removing them does NOT break
```

###

Standard JSON does not allow comments, but `devcontainer.json` is **JSONC** (JSON with Comments), so a `//` note can record a decision next to the code it affects. The Python and Jupyter extensions used to be in the list and were removed to keep the Activity Bar down to the few icons the course uses. Python itself still works. `quarto render` runs the Python chunks in a `.qmd` through the image's Jupyter engine from the command line, with no editor extension involved. What went away is the in-editor layer: notebook tabs, run buttons, and code completion for Python.

### Exercise 10

Find the line containing `"r.consolePath"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-8

)
```

###

```{.output}
"r.consolePath": "/usr/local/bin/arf",
```

###

`arf` is a faster stand-in for the default R Terminal --- it starts quicker and handles pasted multi-line code more reliably. `/usr/local/bin/arf` is a fixed location the image always installs it at, so this setting keeps working even if the image changes internally.

### Exercise 11

Find the line containing `"r.plot.backend"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-9
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Find the line containing \"r.plot.backend\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"r.plot.backend": "httpgd",
```

###

By default, R opens plots in a separate window that would be invisible in a Codespace. Naming `httpgd` here sends plots to the **httpgd** tool instead, which streams them into a panel inside VS Code. The extension's own default, `auto`, would pick whichever plot device it happens to find. Naming one keeps every student on the same device.

### Exercise 12

Find the line containing `"r.source.echo"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-10

  "Find the line containing \"r.source.echo\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"r.source.echo": true,
```

###

The Run Source button (▷ in the editor title bar) normally runs a file silently, showing only the final output. This setting makes it run with `echo = TRUE` instead, so each line prints as it executes.

### Exercise 13

Find the line containing `"git.enableSmartCommit"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-11
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Find the line containing \"git.enableSmartCommit\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"git.enableSmartCommit": true,
```

###

Smart commit automatically includes all changed files in the commit when you click the Commit button in the Source Control sidebar --- you do not need to run `git add` separately. This is why clicking Commit in the `codespace-starter` Codespace works without an extra confirmation step, while the Jupyter Notebook devcontainer setup required one.

### Exercise 14

Find the line containing `"files.autoSave"`. Copy and paste it.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-12
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Find the line containing \"files.autoSave\". Copy and paste it.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"files.autoSave": "afterDelay",
```

###

With `"afterDelay"`, VS Code automatically saves open files a short time after you stop typing. This prevents the most common beginner mistake in coding environments: running code that still reflects the last-saved version rather than the current edits.

### Exercise 17

Now leave the `"settings"` block and scroll back up. Find the `"onCreateCommand"` field. Copy and paste that one line.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-15
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Now leave the \"settings\" block and scroll back up. Find the \"onCreateCommand\" field. Copy and paste that one line.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
"onCreateCommand": "bash ${containerWorkspaceFolder}/.devcontainer/setup.sh",
```

###

This line is behind the "✅ YOUR CODESPACE IS READY" banner that greeted you in your first terminal. An `onCreateCommand` runs once, when the container is first built. For this repo that happens during the prebuild, before you ever see the Codespace. The value is the command: `bash` running `setup.sh`, with `${containerWorkspaceFolder}` standing in for the absolute path of the checkout. `setup.sh` does three things. It installs the `connect-repo` command, sets the short prompt you have been typing at, and adds a few lines to `~/.bashrc` that print the banner the first time a terminal opens. Nothing prints during the build itself, because its output goes to a log. That is why your shell prints the banner later rather than this command printing it directly. Earlier versions of the starter used a `postAttachCommand` instead, which runs in a *visible* terminal every time the editor attaches. That opened a second terminal next to the one Codespaces already gives you, and students kept asking why there were two.

### Exercise 18

You might expect a `"postCreateCommand"` field --- a command that runs every time a Codespace is created. There isn't one. Find the comment that begins `NO postCreateCommand right now`. Copy and paste its first four lines.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-16
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "You might expect a \"postCreateCommand\" field -- a command that runs every time a Codespace is created. There isn't one. Find the comment that begins NO postCreateCommand right now. Copy and paste its first four lines.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
// NO postCreateCommand right now — RETIRED 2026-07-30. All course
// packages ship at whatever versions the image baked; the live at-create
// refresh of a course package was removed because the baked version is
// recent enough, making creates faster and GitHub-independent.
```

###

There used to be a `postCreateCommand` here that refreshed the course packages from GitHub every time a Codespace was created. The course packages now ship at whatever versions the image baked, and updates reach students through a new image release plus a bump of the `"image"` pin you found in Exercise 2. That makes Codespace creation faster and independent of GitHub being reachable.

The rest of the comment keeps the old recipe, dormant, in case course content ever again needs to move faster than image releases. It also records why a revived refresh must be a `postCreateCommand` rather than an `onCreateCommand`, the opposite choice from `setup.sh`. Setup can be frozen into the prebuild. A package refresh cannot, since it would fetch whatever was current when the prebuild ran, not when the Codespace was created. The baked packages cover only the course. Anything else you need, you install yourself, by hand or by asking AI.

### Exercise 19

In the R Terminal, run `install.packages("praise")`. CP/CR.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-17
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "In the R Terminal, run install.packages(\"praise\"). CP/CR.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
> install.packages("praise")
Installing package into '/home/ppbds-student/R/library'
(as 'lib' is unspecified)
trying URL 'https://cloud.r-project.org/src/contrib/praise_1.0.0.tar.gz'
Content type 'application/x-gzip' length 6431 bytes
downloaded 6431 bytes

* installing *source* package 'praise' ...
** package 'praise' successfully unpacked and MD5 sums checked
** using staged installation
** R
** byte-compile and prepare package for lazy loading
** help
*** installing help indices
** building package indices
** testing if installed package can be loaded from temporary location
** testing if installed package can be loaded from final location
** DONE (praise)
```

###

`install.packages()` is base R's package manager: it downloads one package from CRAN and compiles or unpacks it into your library, one call at a time. Contrast this with **pak**: pak resolves and installs entire dependency trees in parallel, which is why the image build (and the dormant refresh recipe you read in Exercise 18) uses `pak::pkg_install()` for the four course packages.

### Exercise 20

In the bash Terminal, run `/opt/venv/bin/pip install emoji`. CP/CR.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-18
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "In the bash Terminal, run /opt/venv/bin/pip install emoji. CP/CR.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
codespace-starter $ /opt/venv/bin/pip install emoji
Collecting emoji
  Downloading emoji-2.14.0-py3-none-any.whl (590 kB)
Installing collected packages: emoji
Successfully installed emoji-2.14.0
```

###

`/opt/venv` is a **virtual environment**: a self-contained folder of Python packages (numpy, pandas, matplotlib, and more) baked into the image and kept separate from the system Python. It is also first on your `PATH`, so plain `pip` already resolves to `/opt/venv/bin/pip`. Naming the full path makes the target explicit, a habit that pays off on machines with more than one Python. Either way the package lands in the environment `quarto render` uses for Python chunks, so `import emoji` works immediately.

### Exercise 22

Ask AI to install the Python library `pyfiglet` into this Codespace's Python environment, and to tell you exactly what command it ran. CP/CR.

```{r}
#| label: codespace-starter-20
#| echo: false
learnr2::question(
  "Ask AI to install the Python library pyfiglet into this Codespace's Python environment, and to tell you exactly what command it ran. CP/CR.",
  type = "reflection",
  show_text = FALSE
)
```

###

```{.output}
codespace-starter $ /opt/venv/bin/pip install pyfiglet
Collecting pyfiglet
  Downloading pyfiglet-1.0.2-py3-none-any.whl (1.1 MB)
Installing collected packages: pyfiglet
Successfully installed pyfiglet-1.0.2
```

###

A good AI agent in this Codespace targets `/opt/venv/bin/pip`, the environment `quarto render` uses for Python chunks (Exercise 20). An agent without that context might install into some other Python and leave `import pyfiglet` failing later. Check which `pip` ran before trusting the result.

## Summary

This tutorial toured the `devcontainer.json` behind `codespace-starter` itself: its pinned custom PPBDS image, its VS Code extensions array, the settings that control the R Terminal, plot rendering, Git commits, autosave, word wrap, and tab behavior, the `onCreateCommand` behind the ready banner, and the retired `postCreateCommand` --- course packages now ship baked into the image, with the refresh recipe kept dormant in a comment. The next tutorial, "The Devcontainer Dockerfile," goes one level deeper and reads through the Dockerfile that actually builds the `ghcr.io/ppbds/devcontainer` image this `devcontainer.json` points at.
